svg.text: Labels with the same name are connected
R30–R33 in series = 4 MΩ feedback resistor
Bridge JP1 with a jumper wire → minutes ~1 per second
Bridge JP2 with a jumper wire → hours ~1 per 3.5 s
→ resets it to 0; its Q3 falling ticks the minutes
→ resets it to 0; its Q3 falling ticks the hours
Hours reach 24 (tens Q2 and ones Q3 high)
U10D unused: tie pins 12 and 13 to GND, leave pin 11 open.
4 · Decoders and displays (CD4511 → 470–680 Ω per segment → 5161AS common-cathode)
C3–C12: 100 nF each, one per chip, placed right beside its power pins (VDD 16 / VSS 8; on U10: 14 / 7).
Bridge the rails of both breadboards together: +5V to +5V, GND to GND.
• A digit ticks when the digit before it rolls over: ones use Q4 falling (9→0),
tens use Q3 falling (6→0 reset). CLK pins on those counters are tied to GND.
• Seconds are counted (U2-B, U3-A) but not shown. DS2’s DP blinks at 1 Hz.
• Tie every unused input to +5V or GND. Floating CMOS inputs cause random jumps.
• Pinout shown is the common 5161AS. Check your display’s pins before wiring.
• Time is random at power-up: bridge JP2 (hours), then JP1 (minutes).
• The 1 Hz decimal point is dim (counter output is weak). That’s expected.
